scenes.title: Designing a Streaming Data Platform
scenes.subtitle: Composing the pieces into a coherent whole
scenes.narration: Designing a streaming platform means composing ingestion, processing, storage, and governance around Kafka as the central nervous system.

scenes.title: The Architectural Layers
bullets: Ingestion via Connect, CDC, and producers
Processing with Streams, Flink, or Spark
Serving to warehouses, lakes, and applications
Governance through schemas, lineage, and access control
scenes.narration: A mature platform has distinct layers. Ingestion brings data in through Kafka Connect, change data capture, and application producers. Processing transforms and enriches streams using Kafka Streams, Flink, or Spark. The serving layer delivers results to warehouses, lakes, and live applications. Wrapping it all is governance, with schema enforcement, data lineage, and access control keeping the platform trustworthy.

scenes.title: End-to-End Data Flow
scenes.narration: Data flows through the platform in a clear path. Sources such as databases, services, and devices emit events. Kafka acts as the durable, replayable backbone that decouples everyone. Stream processors read from Kafka, transform data in flight, and write results back. Sink connectors and applications then serve those results for analytics and real-time features.

scenes.title: Two Guiding Architectures
scenes.narration: Two architectures often guide these designs. The Lambda architecture runs separate batch and speed layers, which duplicates logic and forces you to reconcile their outputs. The Kappa architecture uses a single streaming pipeline and simply replays the Kafka log when it needs to reprocess history. Kappa is simpler to operate and has become the preferred model where the streaming engine is powerful enough.

scenes.title: Naming and Governance Conventions
scenes.code:
# Consistent topic naming: <domain>.<entity>.<event>
#   sales.orders.created
#   sales.orders.updated
#   inventory.stock.adjusted

# Enforce schemas at the registry
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8081/config \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"compatibility": "FULL"}'
scenes.narration: Governance starts with conventions. A consistent topic naming scheme, such as domain, entity, then event, makes the platform navigable as it grows. Setting the schema registry to full compatibility at the cluster level forces every schema change to remain both backward and forward compatible. These guardrails let dozens of teams build on the same platform without breaking one another.

scenes.text: Treat Kafka as the single source of truth and design for replay. If you can reprocess from the log, you can evolve, backfill, and recover with confidence.
scenes.narration: The guiding design principle is to treat Kafka as the single source of truth and design for replay. If you can reprocess from the log, you can evolve, backfill, and recover with confidence.
